detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add optional reward.run_max_concurrent to bound cooperative async scorers across the workers owned by one RewardLoopManager. Two workers with local max_concurrent=2 reach a peak of four without a shared limit and two with run_max_concurrent=2. An unnamed, non-restarting Ray coordinator owns idempotent grants. The controller validates configuration without loading the scorer module; scorer loading and async validation remain in reward workers.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [focused query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20%22run_max_concurrent%22). Refreshed on 2026-10-17 against main `18cfb74852a0`.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

Existing rate_limited concurrency/RPM/TPM limits are process-local. #5327 changes a SearchTool limiter actor's lifetime; #8015 repairs a math_verify process pool; #8101 fixes reward input padding. None implements manager-wide async scorer admission. No issue-closing claim is made.

### Test

Agent-run CPU validation: **38 passed**. The test command is:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/experimental/reward_loop/test_run_reward_budget_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/reward_loop/test_async_token_bucket_on_cpu.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Pre-commit: all 14 upstream hooks passed.

The review regressions use a scorer module that raises if imported in the controller. Both shared-budget scenarios fail on the previous implementation. After the fix, real workers load an async scorer and preserve peak concurrency 4 without the limit and 2 with it; real workers still reject a synchronous scorer when the shared budget is enabled.



WSL Ubuntu, uv-managed Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.12.1, Ray 2.55.1. Installed CPU/test dependencies match the current uv.lock; Megatron-Core's source dependency was omitted. This is not a complete frozen environment or official CI/GPU result. The existing CPU workflow discovers the new `*_on_cpu.py` tests; no workflow change is required.

### API, Design and Boundaries

Set reward.reward_manager.name=rate_limited, an async custom_reward_function, and reward.run_max_concurrent=4. Default null preserves behavior. Admission has its own reward.timeout, then the scorer timeout starts. This is not a hard end-to-end deadline: cancellation still drains in-flight coordinator RPCs and scorer cleanup, and timeout=null keeps unlimited waits. Admission/coordinator failure propagates; scorer exceptions retain existing zero-reward semantics. Cancellation drains scorer cleanup before release. Worker hard death conservatively retains its grant; a later admission timeout requests a job restart after checking outstanding requests, never silently reissues potentially active external work. RPM/TPM stay local; no FIFO fairness, detached-task accounting, or account-wide HTTP quota is promised. Tests use real Ray workers plus deterministic local race controls, without paid APIs or models.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the implementation, documentation, tests and local execution evidence. The contributor reviewed the initial submission, then explicitly requested the review follow-up fixes, test execution, PR updates and reviewer replies. Codex implemented and tested those follow-up changes. Test execution is attributed to Codex, not described as personally performed by the contributor.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md.
- [x] Apply all upstream pre-commit checks.
- [x] Update documentation and add CPU tests covered by the existing workflow.
- [x] Contributor reviewed the initial submission and explicitly requested these review follow-up fixes.
- [x] Relevant tests rerun by Codex at the contributor's explicit request; execution is attributed above.
- [ ] Request CI through the upstream ci-request channel when ready. No message has been sent.

@@ -21,6 +21,65 @@ Key features include:
 2. **Support for hybrid reward settings**, including both generative and discriminative reward models, as well as more complex reward scenarios.
 3. **Simple and extensible interface**, for easily defining customized reward functions.
 
+Sharing an Async Scorer Concurrency Budget
+-----------------------------------------
+
+``rate_limited`` uses process-local semaphores and token buckets. With two
+workers and ``max_concurrent=2``, up to four scorers can be active at once.
+An optional ``reward.run_max_concurrent`` adds one shared concurrency budget
+for all workers owned by the same ``RewardLoopManager``:
+
+.. code-block:: bash
+
+    reward.reward_manager.name=rate_limited \
+    reward.custom_reward_function.path=/path/to/async_judge.py \
+    reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score \
+    reward.run_max_concurrent=4 \
+    +reward.max_concurrent=4
+
+The function must be an ``async def`` custom scorer that cooperatively awaits
+and cleans up its work. The default ``run_max_concurrent=null`` preserves
+existing behavior. A positive integer enables a manager-owned Ray coordinator;
+zero, negative, boolean, and non-integer values are rejected. Other reward
+manager implementations and synchronous scorers are not supported by this
+option. A timed-out synchronous executor thread can continue running after
+its caller returns, so treating it as completed would free capacity too early.
+
+The shared budget is acquired after the local RPM/TPM/concurrency limiters.
+A grant remains occupied until the scorer and its cancellation cleanup finish.
+Waiting for shared capacity has its own ``reward.timeout`` deadline. An
+admission timeout propagates to the caller instead of becoming a zero reward;
+the scorer's separate timeout begins only after admission. RPM and TPM are
+still process-local; this setting does not provide account-wide API quotas,
+FIFO fairness, or coordination between separate RewardLoopManager instances.
+This is not a hard end-to-end deadline: cancellation still waits for in-flight
+coordinator RPCs and scorer cleanup, so an unresponsive coordinator need not
+recover within a bounded time. ``reward.timeout=null`` retains unlimited waits.
+
+The coordinator is unnamed, owned by the current run, and cannot restart with
+an empty grant set. Coordinator errors propagate to the caller rather than
+being converted into a zero reward. If a worker dies while holding a grant,
+the grant is retained and later admission may time out; check outstanding
+scorer requests and restart the job to recover. There is deliberately no lease expiry that could admit new work
+while an old external request is still running. A dead coordinator also
+requires restarting the job.
+
+The guarantee concerns active scorer coroutines. The scorer owns cancellation
+of its external calls: detached tasks, multiple simultaneous requests inside
+one scorer, or a server continuing work after client cancellation cannot be
+counted automatically. These require a service-level admission policy.
+
+The CPU suite uses two real Ray RewardLoopWorkers, a locally saved tokenizer,
+and an instrumented async judge. It observes four simultaneous scorers under
+the legacy per-process limit and two under a shared limit of two. Separate
+tests exercise cancellation during acquisition/release, scorer timeout and
+cleanup, admission timeout, worker death, and coordinator failure. It needs no model download or paid API:
+
+.. code-block:: bash
+
+    uv run --frozen --all-packages --extra cpu pytest -q \
+      tests/experimental/reward_loop/test_run_reward_budget_on_cpu.py
+
 Distributed Reward manager
 --------------------------

+"""Real two-worker budget enforcement and deterministic cancellation races."""
+
+import asyncio
+import os
+import time
+import uuid
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import ray
+import torch
+from omegaconf import OmegaConf
+from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models
+from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
+
+from verl import DataProto
+from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_budget import (
+    RewardConcurrencyBudget,
+    create_reward_budget,
+    run_concurrency_limit,
+    shared_reward_slot,
+)
+from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_loop import RewardLoopManager
+from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager.limited import RateLimitedRewardManager
+
+
+def _data(count=1):
+    return DataProto.from_dict(
+        tensors={
+            "responses": torch.ones(count, 1, dtype=torch.long),
+            "attention_mask": torch.ones(count, 2, dtype=torch.long),
+        },
+        non_tensors={
+            "data_source": np.array(["test"] * count),
+            "reward_model": np.array([{"ground_truth": "answer"} for _ in range(count)], dtype=object),
+            "extra_info": np.array([{"sample": i} for i in range(count)], dtype=object),
+        },
+    )
+
+
+class _LocalRPC:
+    """Controllable transport for race tests; distributed enforcement is tested below."""
+
+    def __init__(self, state):
+        async def acquire(token):
+            return state.try_acquire(token)
+
+        async def release(token):
+            state.release(token)
+
+        self.try_acquire = SimpleNamespace(remote=acquire)
+        self.release = SimpleNamespace(remote=release)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid", [0, -1, True, 1.5, "2"])
+def test_invalid_limits_are_rejected(invalid):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive integer"):
+        run_concurrency_limit({"run_max_concurrent": invalid})
+
+
+def test_budget_is_idempotent_and_independent():
+    first, second = RewardConcurrencyBudget(1), RewardConcurrencyBudget(1)
+    assert first.try_acquire("a")
+    assert first.try_acquire("a")
+    assert not first.try_acquire("b")
+    assert second.try_acquire("b")
+    first.release("unknown")
+    assert not first.try_acquire("b")
+    first.release("a")
+    first.release("a")
+    assert first.try_acquire("b")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("phase", ["acquire", "waiting", "scoring", "release"])
+def test_cancellation_does_not_overtake_pending_grant_or_release(phase):
+    async def scenario():
+        state = RewardConcurrencyBudget(1)
+        rpc = _LocalRPC(state)
+        entered, continue_rpc = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()
+        original_acquire, original_release = rpc.try_acquire.remote, rpc.release.remote
+        if phase == "waiting":
+            assert state.try_acquire("occupied")
+
+        async def acquire(token):
+            if phase in ("acquire", "waiting"):
+                entered.set()
+            if phase == "acquire":
+                await continue_rpc.wait()
+            return await original_acquire(token)
+
+        async def release(token):
+            if phase == "release":
+                entered.set()
+                await continue_rpc.wait()
+            await original_release(token)
+
+        rpc.try_acquire.remote, rpc.release.remote = acquire, release
+
+        async def run():
+            async with shared_reward_slot(rpc):
+                if phase == "scoring":
+                    entered.set()
+                    await asyncio.Event().wait()
+
+        task = asyncio.create_task(run())
+        await asyncio.wait_for(entered.wait(), 2)
+        task.cancel()
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        if phase in ("acquire", "release"):
+            assert not task.done()
+            task.cancel()  # Repeated cancellation must not abandon cleanup.
+            continue_rpc.set()
+        with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+            await asyncio.wait_for(task, 2)
+        assert state.active == ({"occupied"} if phase == "waiting" else set())
+
+    asyncio.run(scenario())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("outcome", ["ok", "error", "timeout", "cancel", "cancel_twice"])
+def test_scorer_cleanup_finishes_before_releasing_capacity(monkeypatch, outcome):
+    async def scenario():
+        monkeypatch.setattr(RateLimitedRewardManager, "_class_initialized", False)
+        state = RewardConcurrencyBudget(1)
+        entered, cleanup_started, finish_cleanup = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()
+
+        async def score(**kwargs):
+            entered.set()
+            try:
+                if outcome in ("timeout", "cancel", "cancel_twice"):
+                    await asyncio.Event().wait()
+                if outcome == "error":
+                    raise RuntimeError("judge failed")
+                return 1.0
+            finally:
+                cleanup_started.set()
+                await finish_cleanup.wait()
+
+        manager = RateLimitedRewardManager(
+            OmegaConf.create({"reward": {"run_max_concurrent": 1, "timeout": 0.1 if outcome == "timeout" else 30}}),
+            SimpleNamespace(decode=lambda *a, **k: "answer"),
+            score,
+            reward_budget=_LocalRPC(state),
+        )
+        task = asyncio.create_task(manager.run_single(_data()))
+        await asyncio.wait_for(entered.wait(), 2)
+        if outcome.startswith("cancel"):
+            task.cancel()
+        await asyncio.wait_for(cleanup_started.wait(), 2)
+        if outcome == "cancel_twice":
+            task.cancel()
+            for _ in range(10):
+                await asyncio.sleep(0)
+            assert not task.done(), "caller must wait for scorer cleanup even after repeated cancellation"
+        assert len(state.active) == 1
+        assert not state.try_acquire("other")
+        finish_cleanup.set()
+        if outcome.startswith("cancel"):
+            with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+                await task
+        else:
+            result = await task
+            assert result["reward_score"] == (1.0 if outcome == "ok" else 0.0)
+            if outcome != "ok":
+                assert result["reward_extra_info"][outcome]
+        assert not state.active
+
+    asyncio.run(scenario())
+
+
+def test_default_is_unchanged_and_unsupported_config_is_rejected(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ray, "remote", lambda *a, **k: pytest.fail("must not create coordinator"))
+    assert create_reward_budget(OmegaConf.create({"reward": {}})) is None
+    config = OmegaConf.create(
+        {"reward": {"run_max_concurrent": 2, "reward_manager": {"source": "register", "name": "naive"}}}
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="registered rate_limited"):
+        create_reward_budget(config)
+    config.reward.reward_manager.name = "rate_limited"
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="custom async"):
+        create_reward_budget(config)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Manager-owned"):
+        RateLimitedRewardManager(config, SimpleNamespace(), lambda **kwargs: 1.0)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="custom async"):
+        RateLimitedRewardManager(config, SimpleNamespace(), lambda **kwargs: 1.0, reward_budget=object())
+
+
+def _observer_class():
+    # A local class is serialized by value; workers need not import the pytest module.
+    class Observer:
+        def __init__(self):
+            self.active = 0
+            self.peak = 0
+            self.pids = set()
+            self.gate = asyncio.Event()
+
+        async def enter(self, pid):
+            self.active += 1
+            self.peak = max(self.peak, self.active)
+            self.pids.add(pid)
+
+        async def leave(self):
+            self.active -= 1
+
+        async def wait(self):
+            await self.gate.wait()
+
+        async def release(self):
+            self.gate.set()
+
+        async def snapshot(self):
+            return self.active, self.peak, self.pids
+
+    return Observer
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def ray_runtime():
+    ray.init(num_cpus=2, include_dashboard=False, object_store_memory=128 * 1024 * 1024, logging_level="ERROR")
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        ray.shutdown()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("run_limit", "is_async"), [(None, True), (2, True), (2, False)])
+def test_real_workers_load_scorer_and_enforce_one_run_budget(tmp_path, ray_runtime, run_limit, is_async):
+    """Load worker-only scorers in workers, rejecting sync scorers with a shared budget."""
+    tokenizer_path = tmp_path / "tokenizer"
+    PreTrainedTokenizerFast(
+        tokenizer_object=Tokenizer(models.WordLevel({"answer": 1, "[UNK]": 0}, unk_token="[UNK]")), unk_token="[UNK]"
+    ).save_pretrained(tokenizer_path)
+    observer_name = "reward-budget-observer-" + uuid.uuid4().hex
+    observer = ray.remote(num_cpus=0)(_observer_class()).options(name=observer_name).remote()
+    scorer = tmp_path / "async_score.py"
+    scorer.write_text(
+        "import os\nimport ray\n"
+        f"if os.getpid() == {os.getpid()}:\n"
+        "    raise RuntimeError('scorer must only be imported in a reward worker')\n"
+        "async def compute_score(observer_name, **kwargs):\n"
+        "    observer = ray.get_actor(observer_name)\n"
+        "    await observer.enter.remote(os.getpid())\n"
+        "    try:\n"
+        "        await observer.wait.remote()\n"
+        "        return 1.0\n"
+        "    finally:\n"
+        "        await observer.leave.remote()\n"
+    )
+    if not is_async:
+        with scorer.open("a") as stream:
+            stream.write("def compute_score(observer_name, **kwargs):\n    return 1.0\n")
+    config = OmegaConf.create(
+        {
+            "actor_rollout_ref": {"model": {"tokenizer_path": str(tokenizer_path), "path": str(tokenizer_path)}},
+            "reward": {
+                "num_workers": 2,
+                "max_concurrent": 2,
+                "run_max_concurrent": run_limit,
+                "timeout": 60,
+                "reward_model": {"enable": False},
+                "reward_manager": {"source": "register", "name": "rate_limited"},
+                "custom_reward_function": {
+                    "path": str(scorer),
+                    "name": "compute_score",
+                    "reward_kwargs": {"observer_name": observer_name},
+                },
+            },
+        }
+    )
+    manager = RewardLoopManager(config)
+    if not is_async:
+        for worker in manager.reward_loop_workers:
+            with pytest.raises(ray.exceptions.RayActorError, match="custom async reward function"):
+                ray.get(worker.__ray_ready__.remote(), timeout=30)
+        return
+    pending = [worker.compute_score_batch.remote(_data(2)) for worker in manager.reward_loop_workers]
+    expected_peak = 4 if run_limit is None else run_limit
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
+    while True:
+        active, peak, pids = ray.get(observer.snapshot.remote(), timeout=5)
+        if active >= expected_peak:
+            break
+        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, (active, peak, pids)
+        time.sleep(0.05)
+    ray.get(observer.release.remote(), timeout=5)
+    results = ray.get(pending, timeout=30)
+    assert [item["reward_score"] for batch in results for item in batch] == [1.0] * 4
+    active, peak, pids = ray.get(observer.snapshot.remote(), timeout=5)
+    assert active == 0
+    assert peak == expected_peak
+    assert len(pids) == 2 and os.getpid() not in pids
+
+
+def test_dead_coordinator_fails_instead_of_becoming_zero_reward(ray_runtime, monkeypatch):
+    async def scenario():
+        monkeypatch.setattr(RateLimitedRewardManager, "_class_initialized", False)
+        budget = ray.remote(num_cpus=0, max_restarts=0)(RewardConcurrencyBudget).remote(1)
+        assert await budget.try_acquire.remote("probe")
+        ray.kill(budget, no_restart=True)
+
+        async def score(**kwargs):
+            pytest.fail("a dead coordinator must not admit scorer work")
+
+        manager = RateLimitedRewardManager(
+            OmegaConf.create({"reward": {"run_max_concurrent": 1}}),
+            SimpleNamespace(decode=lambda *a, **k: "answer"),
+            score,
+            reward_budget=budget,
+        )
+        with pytest.raises(ray.exceptions.RayActorError):
+            await asyncio.wait_for(manager.run_single(_data()), 10)
+
+    asyncio.run(scenario())
+
+
+def test_admission_timeout_is_not_a_zero_reward(monkeypatch):
+    async def scenario():
+        monkeypatch.setattr(RateLimitedRewardManager, "_class_initialized", False)
+        state = RewardConcurrencyBudget(1)
+        assert state.try_acquire("busy")
+
+        async def score(**kwargs):
+            pytest.fail("unadmitted scorer must not start")
+
+        manager = RateLimitedRewardManager(
+            OmegaConf.create({"reward": {"run_max_concurrent": 1, "timeout": 0.05}}),
+            SimpleNamespace(decode=lambda *a, **k: "answer"),
+            score,
+            reward_budget=_LocalRPC(state),
+        )
+        with pytest.raises(TimeoutError, match="shared reward budget"):
+            await asyncio.wait_for(manager.run_single(_data()), 2)
+        assert state.active == {"busy"}
+
+    asyncio.run(scenario())
+
+
+def test_worker_death_does_not_reissue_its_capacity(ray_runtime):
+    class Worker:
+        async def hold(self, budget):
+            return await budget.try_acquire.remote("dead-worker")
+
+    budget = ray.remote(num_cpus=0, max_restarts=0)(RewardConcurrencyBudget).remote(1)
+    worker = ray.remote(num_cpus=0, max_restarts=0)(Worker).remote()
+    assert ray.get(worker.hold.remote(budget), timeout=10)
+    ray.kill(worker, no_restart=True)
+
+    async def scenario():
+        with pytest.raises(TimeoutError, match="Restart the job"):
+            async with shared_reward_slot(budget, timeout=0.1):
+                pytest.fail("a dead worker's external work may still be running")
+        assert not await budget.try_acquire.remote("replacement")
+
+    asyncio.run(scenario())

+"""A manager-owned concurrency budget for cooperative async reward scorers."""
+
+import asyncio
+import uuid
+from contextlib import asynccontextmanager, suppress
+
+import ray
+
+
+def run_concurrency_limit(reward_config) -> int | None:
+    """Validate the optional cross-worker limit without changing legacy defaults."""
+    limit = reward_config.get("run_max_concurrent")
+    if limit is not None and (type(limit) is not int or limit <= 0):
+        raise ValueError("reward.run_max_concurrent must be a positive integer or null")
+    return limit
+
+
+class RewardConcurrencyBudget:
+    """Serialize nonblocking grants in one Ray actor; never reset active grants.
+
+    Calls are idempotent by token. A worker that dies while holding a grant
+    leaves it occupied: automatically expiring it could admit new work while
+    the original external request is still running. Restart the job to recover.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, limit: int):
+        self.limit = run_concurrency_limit({"run_max_concurrent": limit})
+        if self.limit is None:
+            raise ValueError("A shared reward budget requires a limit")
+        self.active: set[str] = set()
+
+    def try_acquire(self, token: str) -> bool:
+        """Grant immediately when capacity is available; do not queue actor calls."""
+        if token in self.active:
+            return True
+        if len(self.active) >= self.limit:
+            return False
+        self.active.add(token)
+        return True
+
+    def release(self, token: str) -> None:
+        """Release a grant, including an unknown/already released token."""
+        self.active.discard(token)
+
+
+def create_reward_budget(config):
+    """Create one unnamed, non-restarting coordinator for this RewardLoopManager."""
+    limit = run_concurrency_limit(config.reward)
+    if limit is None:
+        return None
+    manager = config.reward.reward_manager
+    if manager.source != "register" or manager.name != "rate_limited":
+        raise ValueError("reward.run_max_concurrent requires the registered rate_limited reward manager")
+    from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager.limited import RateLimitedRewardManager
+    from verl.trainer.ppo.reward import resolve_reward_manager_cls
+
+    if resolve_reward_manager_cls(config) is not RateLimitedRewardManager:
+        raise ValueError("reward.run_max_concurrent requires the built-in RateLimitedRewardManager")
+    # Import and validate the scorer in reward workers, where its runtime context is available.

`RewardLoopManager` creates the budget before starting reward workers. `create_reward_budget` calls `get_custom_reward_fn(config)`, which executes the configured module. # Contributor License Agreement (CLA) assistant

Streamline your workflow and let CLA assistant handle the legal side of contributions to a repository for you. CLA assistant enables contributors to sign CLAs from within a pull request.

To get started, simply store your CLA as a GitHub Gist file then link it with the repository/organisation in CLA assistant. Then sit back and relax while CLA assistant:

- Comments on each opened pull request to ask the contributor to sign the CLA
- Allows contributors to sign a CLA from within a pull request
- Authenticates the signee with their GitHub account
- Updates the status of a pull request when the contributor agrees to the CLA
- Automatically asks users to re-sign the CLA for each new pull request in the event the associated Gist & CLA has changed
- Green lights merge queues without additional CLA checks as everyone needs to have signed of on the PR level already

Repository owners can review a list of users who signed the CLA for each version of it. To get started, visit [cla-assistant.io](https://cla-assistant.io).
